title: Dustwallow Marsh
body: Dustwallow Marsh is a fog-bound swamp on the eastern coast of Kalimdor, its western hills dividing it from the Barrens and the sea washing its shores to the north and east. Raptors, spiders, crocolisks and murlocs prowl its reeds, and for ages the marsh belonged to its beasts and to the Stonemaul ogres. Then, after the Third War, Jaina Proudmoore brought the survivors of her expedition to this coast and raised the island city of Theramore, guarded by watchtowers along the road west. The peace has never been easy. Daelin Proudmoore fell at Theramore when his fleet came against the Horde, and some of his loyal marines have since deserted their posts. The Stonemaul ogres, driven from their southern village by black dragonkin, now hold Brackenwall Village for the Horde. Grimtotem tauren have pushed into the north, goblins of the Steamwheedle Cartel trade at Mudsprocket, and in the Wyrmbog to the south Onyxia, daughter of Deathwing, broods in her lair.

title: Theramore Isle
body: Theramore stands on a rocky isle off the coast, a walled city of stone founded by the humans, dwarves and high elves who followed Jaina Proudmoore to Kalimdor after the battle of Mount Hyjal. Her mage tower rises at its heart, Foothold Citadel to the east, and the docks reach out into Dustwallow Bay, where Kul Tiras marines come and go on their monthly pay. A cook gathers swamp recipes for his uncle's restaurant in Stormwind, the physicians of Alliance Trauma train their surgeons here, and an engineer means to relight the old lighthouse to the east. Just north of the gates lies the graveyard, where the Hyal family monument stands among the stones.

title: Foothold Citadel
body: Foothold Citadel is the great stone barracks of Theramore, standing east of Lady Jaina's tower with training grounds at its doors, where guards spar against dummies and drill under their combat masters. Commander Samaul, entirely loyal to his lady, commands her forces from within. On the top floor Captain Garran Vimes runs the city guard and its investigations, Adjutant Tesoran keeps the records of every soldier and every piece of equipment, and Clerk Lendry answers questions about the citizens. The guards here call themselves the finest Alliance soldiers in Kalimdor, sworn to uphold Alliance law so far from home, though the ledgers also list men gone missing, a polite word, Vimes says, for traitors.

title: Sentry Point
body: Sentry Point is the first of Theramore's watchtowers on the road north out of the city, a stone tower and a handful of guards keeping an eye on the marsh and the coast. Captain Wymor commands here, a man who openly sizes up every newcomer. His scouts brought back the strangest report the garrison had heard in years: survivors of a shipwreck walking the Dreadmurk Shore, all of them wearing the red bandanas of the Defias. When Elling Trias's agents came hunting the traitor Hendel during the search for the missing diplomat, this tower was where they looked first.

title: Dreadmurk Shore
body: The Dreadmurk Shore runs north of Theramore's walls, a coast of mud flats, reeds and offshore islets where Mirefin murlocs keep their camps. Among them lurks Razorspine, a murloc who carries a great sword, and the hulking Mudrock turtles that crawl the sand are hunted by Theramore's cooks for their forked tongues. Lately the shore has new tenants. A ship was wrecked off the coast, and its survivors, wearing Defias red, now camp on the islands under their leader Garn Mathers, sending divers and conjurors to search the sunken wreckage. An SI:7 salvage diver, Renn McGill, works the same waters, determined to reach the cargo first.

title: Alcaz Island
body: Alcaz Island lies off the northeastern coast, a lush, tropical isle ruled by the Strashaz naga. Sirens, myrmidons and great hydras guard its shores, and the Tidelord Rrurgaz commands them from behind barred gates. The naga are not alone. The criminal mastermind Doctor Weavil, sworn enemy of the seer Narain Soothfancy, has landed his flying machine here with a band of minions, and fire drakes of the black dragonflight wheel above the island. When Theramore surveyed it from the air it found a rune circle and dragonkin at work, proof that the Defias who wrecked off this coast were serving a far greater master. The bloodkelp the naga gather is sought by those who practice divination.

title: Witch Hill
body: Witch Hill is a haunted stretch of marsh northwest of Theramore, along the road before it turns west. Pale witch lights drift over the water, and the dead walk here: risen husks and spirits that seem to be every soul who ever lived on this land, not only the last. At its heart stands Swamplight Manor, a lonely house whose owners vanished under mysterious circumstances. Everyone who has settled there since has gone mad, or so Draz'Zilb of Brackenwall says, and its current master, the hermit called Swamp Eye Jarl, shares it with an army of giant marsh frogs. In the shallows grows witchbane, an herb whose smoke, hedge mages claim, can draw evil from its hiding place.

title: North Point Tower
body: North Point Tower is the second outpost on the road north from Theramore, and since the deserters seized Lost Point it has been the most distant of the city's watchtowers. Captain Darill, something of an expert on the Grimtotem tauren, holds it against their raids from Blackhoof Village, while Sergeant Lukas tries to free the patrols they capture and dreams of turning the Bloodfen raptors loose on the tauren camp. The tower holds a prisoner of its own. When a blood elf ship called the Dawn Runner ran aground, Theramore's men seized its cargo and its last surviving crewman, Ithania, and keep both at the top of the tower.

title: Blackhoof Village
body: Blackhoof Village is a large new settlement of the Grimtotem clan, raised near Bluefen in the north of the marsh around a windmill. From here the most warlike of the tauren clans raid the road and the towers of Theramore, and they cage the human soldiers they capture. Grimtotem elders keep battle plans that carry orders from Thunder Bluff, and those plans leave no doubt: the clan means to drive the human settlements from the marsh, Theramore included. Its arms are new work from a Thunder Bluff forge, and none of them has yet seen battle, a sign that the Grimtotem keep other camps in the marsh.

title: Darkmist Cavern
body: Darkmist Cavern was once a mine, cut into the hills northwest of Brackenwall Village, but the miners are long gone and the darkmist spiders have taken it for themselves. Silkspinners and recluses web its tunnels, and few outside the marsh would bother them at all, except that their parts are oddly prized. The blacksmith of Brackenwall uses the acid of their venom sacs to clean burned metal, and the hermit at Swamplight Manor insists that the juice of an unpopped darkmist eye is a fine drink, smooth and salty.

title: Brackenwall Village
body: Brackenwall Village is the Horde's stronghold in Dustwallow Marsh, a rough camp of huts in the northwest where the Stonemaul ogres took refuge after black dragonkin burned them out of their southern home. Overlord Mok'Morokk rules it, though not all his ogres are content: the learned Draz'Zilb refuses to call it home, and old Tharg still mourns the wife the dragons killed. Orcs and trolls of the Horde work alongside them. Krog watches the humans for Orgrimmar, the spymaster Nazeer Bloodpike sends agents against Theramore, whose own infiltrators spy on the village from the reeds to the east, and the stranded blood elf Balandar Brightstar finds the ogres good for little but crude jokes and sour ale.

title: Shady Rest Inn
body: Only a blackened chimney and scattered rubble remain of the Shady Rest Inn, on the road where Dustwallow meets the Barrens. James Hyal built it, one of those who came across the sea with Lady Proudmoore, dreaming of a fine stopping place for travelers, and for a while it prospered. Then Theramore lost control of the marsh roads, and James was too stubborn to retreat behind the city's walls. The inn was burned to the ground, and his wife and son were killed. Investigators from Theramore and Brackenwall have both picked through the ashes, and Inspector Tarem dusts the ruins with a powder that makes hidden clues shine.

title: Lost Point
body: Lost Point is a Theramore watchtower that the garrison could no longer hold, standing southeast of the ruined Shady Rest Inn. Abandoned by its soldiers, it has been taken over by deserters from Theramore's own ranks, men whose loyalty to Admiral Daelin Proudmoore outlived the admiral. Their lieutenant, Balos Jacken, keeps them hidden here and wants nothing more than to be forgotten. They are too few to stand against the ogres of Brackenwall and avoid trouble with them, and they cast out one of their own, a former lieutenant named Paval Reethe, for raiding the ogres' supplies once too often.

title: Tabetha's Farm
body: In the heart of the Quagmire, beside the road south of North Point Tower, stands the small farm of Tabetha, a hermit mage who has trained generations of apprentices here. Her two current students, Morlann and Garion, bicker endlessly over missing reagents, and Garion nurses a wound from the last Grimtotem raid. Both Theramore and Brackenwall send their people to check on her, for she has kept the peace between them as well as anyone. She has new neighbors now, the Grimtotem of Direhorn Post just to the north, and an SI:7 agent, Andello Porter, has taken up quiet watch at the farm.

title: Direhorn Post
body: Direhorn Post is a Grimtotem war camp just north of Tabetha's Farm, easy to find for the totems its tauren raise to announce themselves. By night its warriors chant of their deeds against everyone who has tried to settle in the marsh, and by day they raid the farm, determined to drive Tabetha and her students out. The camp holds a stranger guest. A Forsaken apothecary named Cylla works among the Grimtotem, and a letter on her from the new masters of Lordaeron pledges aid against their mutual enemy in Kalimdor, a pact that troubles Theramore and the Horde alike.

title: Beezil's Wreck
body: Beezil's Wreck lies east of Tabetha's Farm near the mountains, where a goblin zeppelin piloted by one Beezil came down in the swamp. It was carrying six months of supplies for the new goblin town at Mudsprocket, and what survived the crash is strewn across the marsh as far as the Quagmire, while the broken hull smolders in a heap of twisted metal and burning fuel. The Steamwheedle Cartel has sent Moxie Steelgrille, a wary goblin slow to trust strangers, to salvage what she can, but acidic oozes have gathered around the wreckage and are slowly digesting the cargo before she can reach it.

title: Nat's Landing
body: Across Dustwallow Bay to the southwest, in Tidefury Cove, a small island holds the fishing camp of Nat Pagle, one of the most famous fishermen in Azeroth. Nat's Landing is little more than a small dock to fish from, which suits its owner. The cove around it is busy with Muckshell crab-men, and a wrecked ship lies in the water to the southwest, where Nat sends the brave or foolish to test his newest baits. Anglers who have learned all their own masters can teach come from both Orgrimmar and Ironforge, sent by their own trainers, to sit on this jetty and learn from him.

title: Stonemaul Ruins
body: The Stonemaul Ruins were once the home of the Stonemaul ogres, a village in the south of the marsh with the clan's great mound, now called the Den of Flame, cut into the hills nearby. Then the brood of Onyxia descended on it. The dragonkin slew every Stonemaul who did not flee, and the survivors ran north to Brackenwall, leaving behind their dead, their clan banner and even their overlord's grog, snuff and strongbox. Firemane dragonkin and searing whelps now hold the ruins, ogre bones lie where they fell, and the angry spirits of the Stonemaul dead still rise from them, asking where the rest of their people have gone.

title: Mudsprocket
body: Mudsprocket is the Steamwheedle Cartel's newest outpost, a muddy goblin town in the south of the marsh at the end of the road past Tabetha's Farm and the Stonemaul Ruins. It welcomes Theramore and Horde traders alike and needs every contact it can get, for the zeppelin that should have stocked it crashed in the swamp, leaving it short of food, tools and medicine. Drazzit Dripvalve runs the town on a tight budget and has posted a bounty on Goreclaw the Ravenous, a raptor of the Bloodfen Burrow that has killed two of his engineers. Its oddest resident is Brogg, a Stonemaul ogre who lives in the only building big enough for him and plays dice with the goblins.

title: The Dragonmurk
body: The Dragonmurk is the steaming southern fen where the black dragonflight has made its home, and it takes its name from them. Onyxia's brood has spread across it, and her eggs lie hidden among the reeds, each one another whelp to swell the dragonkin's ranks. Firemane flamecallers and scalebanes stalk the mud, a scorchscale drake circles overhead, and the black drake Brimgore prowls the fen, and Overlord Mok'Morokk's lost strongbox lies somewhere in the muck. Not everything here is deadly. Wyrmtail, a coiled herb that seems to pulse when looked at, grows thick in the Dragonmurk, and Mudsprocket uses it to dull pain and close wounds.

title: Wyrmbog
body: The Wyrmbog is the deepest corner of the south, a reeking marsh at the foot of the hills where the black dragonflight is strongest. Here, behind a cave mouth shaped like a dragon's jaws, lies the lair of Onyxia, the brood mother of the flight, who fled here when her masquerade at the court of Stormwind was undone. Her eggs are hidden all around the entrance, guarded by firemane flamecallers and scorchscale drakes. In a cave of its own nearby dwells the old drake Emberstrife. Challenges shouted at the lair go unanswered by the dragon herself: when an ogre's banner was planted at the gate, only her servant Smolderwing came, to say that Onyxia answers to no one.

title: Lady Jaina Proudmoore
body: Jaina Proudmoore, ruler of Theramore, is the daughter of Admiral Daelin Proudmoore of Kul Tiras and was once the apprentice of Archmage Antonidas of Dalaran. When the Scourge rose, a prophet urged her to lead survivors west across the sea, and in Kalimdor she stood with Thrall and the night elves against Archimonde at Mount Hyjal. Afterward she founded Theramore. When her father came with his fleet to make war on the Horde, she would not fight beside him, and he died at her city. She has worked for peace ever since, even arranging a secret summit between Thrall and King Varian Wrynn, though deserters loyal to her father call her a coward. Her city, she says, must come first.

title: Captain Garran Vimes
body: Captain Garran Vimes commands the Theramore guard from the top floor of Foothold Citadel, proud of his soldiers and of the Alliance law they keep so far from home. He reads Orcish better than most, which makes him the man to see when a Horde spy's report turns up in the mud. Most of his days go to the mysteries of the marsh, chief among them the burning of the Shady Rest Inn, which his men have investigated with little luck. He has a soldier's dry wit about the deserters, who accuse Theramore of betraying the Alliance while they betray it themselves, and a soft spot for poor James Hyal, the innkeeper who lost everything.

title: Smiling Jim
body: The man Theramore calls Smiling Jim stands in the city's inn, grinning and singing the same few lines over and over, a song about a man who served mead and beer from ear to ear and year to year. His real name is James Hyal. He crossed the sea with Lady Proudmoore, a fine cook by his brother's account, and built the Shady Rest Inn at the edge of the Barrens. When it was burned, his wife and son were killed, and James never recovered. The guards pity him and will not speak of it. At the family monument outside the gates, they say, his wife's spirit still waits for him with their little boy.

title: Overlord Mok'Morokk
body: Mok'Morokk rules the Stonemaul ogres at Brackenwall Village, raised to be their overlord by Rexxar himself. Under Rexxar's eye he showed real strength, but once his patron left, power went to his head. When the black dragonkin burned the clan's old home in the south, he ordered his people to run rather than fight, and he insists that the new village is safe because there are no dragons there. He calls himself a smart ogre and a good leader, but he pines most for his grog, his snuff and his strongbox, all abandoned in the flight. Many of his ogres want revenge and their old home. He would rather stay, and even beaten, he still claims to be boss.

title: Krog
body: Krog is an orc of Brackenwall Village and a shrewd agent of Orgrimmar. He boasts that the humans once claimed most of the marsh until the Stonemaul, with Horde help, pushed them back. When the Shady Rest Inn burned, Orgrimmar ordered him to assist the human investigators, and he did, in his way: help them, feed them a tidbit or two, and keep the real findings for the Horde. He has hunters like Kagoro and Ogron to track for him, a set of armor the Earthen Ring gave him in thanks for some past service, and a sense of what the Grimtotem might cost the Horde. Whatever he learns goes straight to the Warchief.

title: Tabetha
body: Tabetha keeps a little farm in the heart of the Quagmire and is far more than the old hermit she seems. She is a mage and scryer of some renown, older than she looks, and she has trained apprentices here for generations, Horde mages among them. Young mages of both sides come to her to earn a mage's wand, warlocks sent by Menara Voidrender bring her a tainted infernal orb whose demon she draws out, and she does not forgive theft: when the hydromancer Velratha of Zul'Farrak stole her Tiara of the Deep, she wanted it back badly. Both Theramore and Brackenwall trust her, and she has done more than most to keep the peace between them.

title: Brogg
body: Brogg is a Stonemaul ogre who fled with Overlord Mok'Morokk when the black dragonkin took the clan's old home, believing they would soon return to fight. The counterattack never came, and when his overlord refused to seek revenge for the friends Brogg had lost, he left Brackenwall for good. The goblins of Mudsprocket let him stay in the only building large enough to hold him, though he sometimes suspects they are laughing at him, and he trades the meat of his hunting trips at their dice table. He has never given up on his people. Brogg means to lay the Stonemaul dead to rest, avenge them, and lead the clan back where it belongs.

title: Swamp Eye Jarl
body: The hermit called Swamp Eye Jarl lives alone at Swamplight Manor, which he took over after its previous owners vanished. Some say he is not quite right in the head, and he does little to argue. He loves swamp cooking above all things, fried frog legs and stews, and drinks the juice of spider eyes, talking fondly to the ones that stare back. He wants a particular swing blade carried by the murloc Razorspine, for some cutting he will not explain, and he tells visitors to get off his lawn unless they mean to help in the kitchen. A sergeant at the Theramore docks sends people to check on him because he reminds her of her grandfather.

title: Nat Pagle
body: Nat Pagle is one of the most famous fishermen in Azeroth, though he claims he does not much enjoy fishing, having done it for twenty or thirty years. To him the best part is the slow pace, time to think about past and future, and a fine excuse to drink, heavily. Master anglers of both the Horde and the Alliance are sent to his island camp in Dustwallow when their own teachers have nothing left to give, and Nat tests them with lists of rare fish from far shores. He swears by a lucky measuring tape and his own foul-smelling baits, and he knows the sailors' tales of sea monsters are true, having seen a few himself.

title: Emberstrife
body: Emberstrife is an ancient drake of the black dragonflight who dwells in a den of his own in the Wyrmbog. He is an old gatekeeper of Nefarian, charged with testing the dragonspawn who would rise to the rank of elite guard to Onyxia. In the name of Deathwing, whom he calls Father, he sets them the Test of Skulls: to slay the drake champions of the lesser flights, Scryer of the blue, Somnus of the green, Chronalis of the bronze and Axtroz of the red. From their skulls he shapes the medallion of a guardian to the brood mother. Champions seeking the Seal of Ascension come instead to break his will and forge it in his flame.

title: Ashes of the Shady Rest
body: Captain Vimes had found nothing in the ashes of the Shady Rest Inn, so others went looking. From the rubble came hoofprints in the mud, a blackened iron shield fixed to the chimney and the badge of Lieutenant Paval Reethe. Adjutant Tesoran's books showed Reethe as a Kul Tiran marine listed missing, and the deserters at Lost Point admitted they had cast him out. The shield's strap, said Theramore's smith, was made for a tauren. Inspector Tarem's work pointed to the Grimtotem, and Captain Darill at North Point sent searchers into Blackhoof Village, where battle plans showed the clan meant to drive every human from the marsh. Yet Blackhoof's weapons had never been used. Tabetha knew why: the guilty band camped beside her farm at Direhorn Post. Their tents burned, and at the Hyal grave the spirits of James's wife and son gave thanks.
sources: creature_text 23768 (Lynn Hyal at the monument)
notes: verified. Faction 1: all entry quests AllowableRaces 1101.

title: The Black Shield
body: Orgrimmar wanted to know who burned the Shady Rest Inn, and that the Alliance should never blame the Horde. Krog sent his trackers after the hoofprints and Ogron after a human named Paval Reethe, whose Theramore badge lay in the ashes. Ogron found the deserter hiding on an island, but before Reethe could talk, an arrow from the reeds struck him down. The blackened shield from the chimney fared better. Acid from darkmist spiders cleaned its rim enough to show the name Mosarn, a smith of Thunder Bluff, who admitted that the Grimtotem were his best customers. His arms filled the new Grimtotem camp at Blackhoof Village, but none had seen battle. Tabetha, who has trained Horde mages, pointed to the true culprits at Direhorn Post, and warned that the Horde cannot afford to leave the Grimtotem unchecked forever. Krog carried it all to Thrall.

title: The Deserters
body: Not every soldier who followed the Proudmoores to Kalimdor followed Jaina's peace. Deserters loyal to the late admiral had slipped agents back into Theramore, chatting up guards at every post, praising Admiral Proudmoore as the true hero and Lady Jaina as a coward. Calia Hastings of SI:7 came to end it. The agitators were exposed, and their leaflets, smuggled in aboard a privateer ship at the farthest dock, were seized from the captain's quarters. Calia rewrote them with a little creative editing, and when the altered pages went round the barracks the guards laughed so hard that no deserter could ever again be taken seriously within the walls. Last came their base, a ship moored on an island southeast of the docks. Their leader, Gavis Greyshield, put up a show of a fight, then surrendered and asked only that his men be spared.

title: Precious Cargo
body: With the deserters broken, Theramore's scouts brought stranger news: men in Defias red, survivors of a shipwreck, on the Dreadmurk Shore. Captain Wymor at Sentry Point had the band's leader, Garn Mathers, slain, and his orders spoke of precious cargo in words that hinted at a wealthy patron. The SI:7 diver Renn McGill, with diving gear borrowed from the Defias, had strongboxes raised from the wreck and found among the coins a pair of enchanted manacles. The cargo had been a person. Lady Jaina ordered Alcaz Island surveyed by gryphon, and the rider saw a rune circle and dragonkin. Then Jaina explained. The prisoner had been King Varian Wrynn himself, bound in secret for a summit she had arranged with Thrall, and the Defias had sold themselves to a far greater master to take him. She had been a fool, she admitted, to think them broken with VanCleef's death.

title: The Beast Beneath the Lighthouse
body: The old lighthouse east of Theramore had been dark for some time when the engineer Babs Fizzletorque decided to relight it. Its log called for oil from the young murk threshers under the docks, and in a trunk upstairs she found a book of sailors' tales, Dastardly Denizens of the Deep, good only for a laugh. The fishmonger Dirty Michael Crowe, who collects old books, did not laugh. Sailors still spoke, he said, of Tethyr, a sea creature living right here. Nat Pagle agreed, once he had tested a foul new bait on the visitor who asked. Tethyr was real, he was drawn to bright light, and he was the reason the lighthouse had been shut down. Major Mills would not risk Theramore's shipping. He mounted mortars on the docks, lined up his marksmen and lit the lamp, and when the beast came the defenders brought it down.

title: The Brood of Onyxia
body: The Stonemaul ogres fled their village in the south when dragons fell upon it, but no one knew whose dragons they were until Draz'Zilb, an ogre mage as learned as he is scornful of his overlord, cast his spells over the hearts and tongues of the whelps. The answer was the brood of Onyxia, daughter of Deathwing, and Draz'Zilb doubted she had come to the marsh merely to besiege a band of ogres. Overlord Mok'Morokk would hear none of it: there were no dragons in Brackenwall. While Tharg, who lost his wife in the attack, sent warriors against the black dragon army for revenge, Draz'Zilb sent others to the Wyrmbog to smash Onyxia's eggs before more could hatch. Then he asked one last service. Mok'Morokk was challenged before his people, beaten, and fled like a frightened child, leaving the clan free to choose a leader who would take them home.

title: Challenge to the Black Flight
body: Brogg had waited long enough for his overlord to avenge the Stonemaul, so from Mudsprocket he set about doing it himself. For his ritual he needed magic feathers from the raptors of the Bloodfen Burrow, and then either the clan banner, left deep in the old mound that the dragonkin now call the Den of Flame, or the essences of the dragonkin who had killed his friends. With these he made a totem, and at the Stonemaul Ruins it drew the restless ogre spirits from their bones so that they could be fought and laid to rest. One task remained. Brogg's banner was carried east to the dragon's-mouth cave of the Wyrmbog and planted before Onyxia's lair as his challenge. The brood mother did not come. Her drake Smolderwing answered in her place, and Brogg decided that, like all her flight, she fights only when victory is certain.

title: The Last Report of Marg Nighteye
body: The Horde and Theramore keep an uneasy truce in the marsh, and Nazeer Bloodpike, the spymaster of Brackenwall, means to come out on top of it. His hunters cull the Alliance infiltrators who watch the village, and his agents dive beneath the Theramore docks for documents thrown into the sea by a spy caught aboard a ship. One of his best, Marg Nighteye, simply vanished while watching the city. His severed hand turned up in the mud still clutching his report, and soon after his head, its ragged wound a mystery. Kin'weelay of Grom'gol called up Marg's furious spirit, which told the tale: a muckshell crab-man had killed him on his way home with a jeweled pendant stolen from a camp of soldiers on the beach. The pendant was a noble's jewel, far richer than any soldier's, and it went to Zor Lonetree in Orgrimmar to be studied.

title: The Haunting of Witch Hill
body: Mordant Grimsby, an herbalist, came out to Swamplight Manor to visit his old friend Jarl with a housewarming gift, and found him babbling about frogs in an empty cabin while the dead walked outside. Mordant would not leave him to it. The risen husks and spirits of Witch Hill, laid to rest one by one, told him that this was no ordinary haunting: they were every soul who had ever lived on the land, corrupted and killed by the same evil, each learning the truth too late. Mordant remembered that hedge mages use the smoke of witchbane to draw evil out of hiding. A torch bound with the herb was planted at the end of the manor's dock, and from the smoke rose Zelfrax, who claimed the land as his long before mortals came. When he fell, Mordant was almost more surprised than relieved. Jarl's taste in furniture, he admitted, remained beyond saving.
